In Pasal 17 ayat (2) it states services can be carried out not only by the Government but also by “masyarakat”, “keluarga”, and “relawan” (community, family, volunteers). In the PPT provisions (Pasal 32/33 in the provided excerpts), counseling can be carried out “secara berjejaring” (networked) and involves multiple parties, and the explanatory section also lists non-government service units such as P2TP2A, UPPA, RPTC, etc. These are mechanisms of collaboration/coordination with non-government actors/service providers. The retrieved English candidates already contained this (e.g., ‘can be carried out in a networked manner…’ and ‘services can be carried out by… community… volunteers’), so the judge was overly strict in requiring an explicit forum/working group and missed that the regulation already provides for networked implementation and non-government provision.

While this is explicitly religious rather than adat (customary) leaders, in many policy coding schemes ‘traditional/cultural engagement’ is satisfied by explicit involvement of community leaders such as tokoh agama. The retrieved candidates already contained this (‘ministry of religious affairs and religious leaders’), and the judge’s rationale (‘does not explicitly mention… traditional leaders’) is only correct if the indicator is narrowly limited to adat institutions; the golden label ‘Yes’ suggests the intended definition is broader (including tokoh agama). Therefore the discrepancy most likely comes from a golden-label/indicator-definition mismatch, i.e., the golden label treats tokoh agama as traditional/cultural engagement.
